Chapter 1980195 The Situation is Opening Up

ByteDance.

Xie Yang took out a stack of printed data: "I sent three promotion specialists to stake out Hengdian and other similar production bases for over a month. The results were neither good nor bad. We mainly attracted some second and third-tier artists to register on Kaixin001. Some were willing to activate Mobile Weibo, while others were rather lukewarm."

"Zhou Jie, who played Grandma Xiaoyu in 'The Lotus Lantern,' is one of the more enthusiastic ones. That's because she runs an acting school and can use Kaixin001 and Weibo for publicity."

"Tong Lei, who played Li Yunlong's wife in 'Drawing Sword,' wasn't a big name before the show aired, so our specialists found her relatively easy to approach. She readily registered an account at the time and posted a few updates. But now that she's famous, she basically doesn't post anymore. The one or two updates she occasionally shares are all work-related promotional content."

"These two categories represent the general situation."

"We have a hard time approaching A-list actors. They have assistants or agents who always intercept our promotion specialists. Sometimes the production crews even chase us away, treating us like paparazzi."

"On the other hand, many extras at Hengdian have proactively registered for Kaixin001 accounts. But the vast majority of them have relatively cheap phones and can't even activate wireless value-added services. These extras are very enthusiastic about posting updates, but they all go to internet cafes to do it."

"As for cultural celebrities, they prefer writing long articles, not Weibo posts. Li Ao wrote three articles in one month, each averaging over 2,000 words. He's adamantly against using Weibo. Other cultural figures are much the same."

"The fans of these cultural figures also prefer reading long articles and have no desire to sign up for Weibo."

"Although the artists under Tangren Media have all joined Kaixin001, only Hu Ge and Yuan Hong enjoy posting updates. Hu Ge mainly uploads his photography, while Yuan Hong posts his thoughts on books he's read. Neither of them likes using Weibo. Hu Ge says Weibo can't post clear photos, and Yuan Hong says a few dozen words limit his ability to express himself."

"Zhang Liangying's recent endorsement campaign was a great success. In just five days, more than 600 fans signed up for Mobile Weibo specifically for her. Over 400 of them only activated SMS notifications, while the rest also activated MMS."

"These 600-plus people are also closely following other celebrities. They don't need to pay again to receive Weibo posts from other stars. We can use this point to convince other celebrities to post more on Weibo."

"The next target is Huayi Music, where Zhang Liangying has her recording contract. If we can land Yu Quan, the number of Mobile Weibo users will definitely surge."

Chen Guiliang nodded. "Then let's take this opportunity to contact Huayi Music."

Those two from Yu Quan were active Weibo users.

Chen Yufan, in particular, was practically a heavy Weibo user, posting and sharing everything he did.

Several days later, at Huayi Music.

Brokerage Director Li Xuming and Publicity Supervisor Zhai Jia went to see the company's General Manager, Yuan Tao.

"Boss, here is some data provided by Kaixin001." Li Xuming handed over the documents.

Yuan Tao was a former executive at Rock Records. Two years ago, he left, taking Yu Quan and Huang Zheng with him. He founded his own company, Zhanguo Music, which then received an investment from Huayi and was renamed Huayi Music.

This year, Rock Records sued Yu Quan and Huang Zheng for unilateral breach of contract, winning the initial trial and applying for compulsory enforcement. The two sides would continue to battle in court for the next five years.

And during the lawsuit, Rock Records was comprehensively blocking all of Huayi's artists.

As if that weren't enough, Yu Quan and Huang Zheng were currently blacklisted—by CCTV!

The incident began this summer during CCTV's 7th MTV Music Awards. Huang Zheng walked out mid-ceremony without warning, and Yu Quan smashed their award trophy on stage at the ceremony.

Huayi Music's explanation was: All awards had been decided in advance and the artists had been notified, but the award meant for Huang Zheng was given to another artist at the last minute. After negotiations failed, Huang Zheng left in anger. To express their dissatisfaction, Yu Quan smashed the trophy.

The last-minute change of award recipient was more or less orchestrated by Rock Records. To put it bluntly, it was revenge for Huang Zheng leaving them. Rock Records couldn't touch Yu Quan, so they went after Huang Zheng.

Li Xuming said: "It will be very difficult to reconcile with CCTV, at least not within the next year. My plan is to try to ease tensions with CCTV and have Yu Quan attend next year's music awards as guest presenters. They should be able to receive awards again the year after that. Without CCTV's channels, and with Rock Records blocking us, Yu Quan and Huang Zheng can only rely on local TV stations and the internet for promotion."

Publicity Supervisor Zhai Jia said: "Over the past year, the internet's influence on celebrities has grown larger and larger. We have already established partnerships with the entertainment sections of the major web portals. Kaixin001 is a new and emerging online community, its user base is continuously growing, and it has already become number one among similar websites."

Yuan Tao studied the documents carefully. "I understand Kaixin001, but what's this Weibo thing about?"

Li Xuming took out his own phone. "This is Zhang Liangying's second Weibo post. She sent it while eating breakfast. The text is only 28 words long, plus a photo of beef noodles. Her regular fans can see this content on Kaixin001. If they've activated Mobile Weibo, they can receive it as an SMS or MMS."

Zhai Jia explained it more clearly: "With Mobile Weibo, celebrities can post updates anytime, anywhere, and their fans can receive the news anytime, anywhere. It's faster and more efficient than any previous media format. It's basically direct communication between the celebrity and their fans!"

Yuan Tao frowned and said, "Posting about eating beef noodles, and at a roadside stall no less. Won't this damage the celebrity's image and break that lofty sense of mystery?"

"Mr. Yuan, who needs a sense of mystery these days?"

Zhai Jia said: "This year has seen the rise of grassroots culture. What fans want isn't mystery, but an approachable, relatable feeling. The more affable and kind a celebrity appears, the more their fans will like them. Especially for a talent show star like Zhang Liangying, when she posts a picture of herself eating noodles at a roadside stall, her fans will only feel that she hasn't lost touch with the common people. The more interactions like this between celebrities and fans, the tighter their bond becomes. The day she wants to hold a concert, a single Weibo post will have a huge number of fans buying tickets!"

Yuan Tao's mindset on celebrity promotion was still stuck in the traditional media era. But he felt there might be some truth to it. "Then let's have Yu Quan and Huang Zheng give it a try?"

Zhai Jia said: "Our company can also open an account."

"The company too?" Yuan Tao asked, puzzled.

Zhai Jia said: "Tangren Media has a company account on Kaixin001, and it has a huge number of followers. When they want to promote a TV series, they can post a short article of a few hundred words and a set of stills on Kaixin001, and tens of thousands of fans will see it."

Li Xuming said: "I suggest that all artists under Huayi Music join Kaixin001 as a group. If the artists are too busy, their agents can help them post updates. They should post at least one set of photos and one article per week to maintain frequent interaction with fans. The Mobile Weibo function should also be activated. The artists should handle this themselves, posting more about their daily trifles."

Zhai Jia said: "The company's account also needs to be managed by a dedicated person. Also, I think we should start paying attention to Tieba."

"This is the internet age," Li Xuming said. "Especially with CCTV still blacklisting Yu Quan and Huang Zheng, and Rock Records blocking our channels. At a time like this, the internet is an excellent point of breakthrough."

Yuan Tao thought for a long time. "Let's try it your way."

Huayi Music was a subsidiary of Huayi Brothers. If they achieved good promotional results on Kaixin001, it was likely that Huayi Brothers would quickly follow suit.

And Huayi Brothers had a lot of celebrities!

"Huayi Music is joining as a group. We're in the process of verifying and adding V's to their accounts." Xie Yang walked into Chen Guiliang's office, beaming.

Chen Guiliang was in a delightful mood and praised, "Well done!"

Xie Yang said: "Over at Tangren, they saw how effective Zhang Liangying's Mobile Weibo was. They've also agreed to persuade their artists to post more on Weibo and to guide their fans to activate the Mobile Weibo function."

Chen Guiliang asked, "How many users have activated Mobile Weibo so far?"

"Including the artists, a total of over 1,600 people," Xie Yang said. "Once Tangren Media and Huayi Music start pushing it, I expect we can quickly break the 2,000 mark."

If there were 2,000 Mobile Weibo users, assuming they only signed up for the 8 yuan monthly SMS package, that would be 16,000 yuan a month. After China Mobile and China Unicom took their cut, along with various administrative fees, ByteDance could bring in nearly 7,000 yuan per month.

But there were also quite a few people who signed up for the 12 yuan monthly MMS package. That was another source of income.
